obligations.statement: Establish progressive disease (PD) of the malignancy being screened at a specific assessment under RECIST version 1.1.
obligations.source_locator: Signed protocol v2 / Amendment 1, p. 48, §5.2.3, item 18. The named standard is protocol reference 3, p. 105.

obligations.statement: Accept qualifying progression in measurable or non-measurable disease. A measurable target lesion is optional. RECIST 1.1 permits overall PD from qualifying target progression, unequivocal non-target progression, or a definite new malignant lesion.
obligations.source_locator: Signed protocol v2 / Amendment 1, p. 48, §5.2.3, item 18 (both disease presentations). Protocol reference 3, §§4.3–4.4.1 and Tables 1–2 (RECIST interpretation).

obligations.statement: Link the progression to actual previous treatment of this patient's same malignancy and establish that progression occurred after the qualifying treatment event.
obligations.source_locator: Signed protocol v2 / Amendment 1, p. 48, §5.2.3, item 18 (sequence). Signed protocol, p. 61, §8.2, screening/baseline assessments, final paragraph (prior systemic and non-systemic treatment with associated disease response).

obligations.statement: Apply a six-month lookback before screening. Which member of the treatment–progression pair must fall in that interval requires interpretation.
obligations.source_locator: Signed protocol v2 / Amendment 1, p. 48, §5.2.3, item 18, final clause. task.json, screening_clock, supplies the workflow screening date.

obligations.statement: At screening, review the history of the current malignancy, including previous treatment, associated response and date of last disease progression. Document the eligibility assessment in the source record.
obligations.source_locator: Signed protocol, p. 61, §8.2. This is the source-review context for item 18.

screening_window.precision: Use the clinical event date. If only same-day dates are available and precedence cannot be established, retain unknown.

predicate.over: associated (assessment, course) pairs for the patient and index malignancy

evidence_semantics.assessment: Use a source-supported overall RECIST 1.1 PD determination, including a documented RECIST reread of historical imaging where available. An isolated measurement, a generic worsening code, symptoms alone or the presence of non-measurable disease does not establish PD.
evidence_semantics.time: Use the effective date assigned to progression. Track the report or review timestamp separately to establish what was known at screening. Preserve actual time or documented ordering when available.
evidence_semantics.source_scope: Section 8.3 and the radiologic evaluation in §8.3.1 (pp. 61–62) describe trial efficacy assessments by investigators with possible Part B central reading. Item 18 does not impose central reading or the on-study imaging schedule on historical assessments.
evidence_semantics.missing_evidence: An absent, conflicting, unevaluable or undated record that could change the result yields unknown. A negative result requires sufficient reviewed history to rule out a qualifying pair. An unrelated treatment or a future record cannot supply a missing fact.

bindings.fact: Overall timepoint PD for this malignancy, with explicit RECIST 1.1 method and coverage of measurable and non-measurable disease.
bindings.proposed_source: A source-linked oncology or radiology response assessment, represented as a final or amended FHIR R4 DiagnosticReport with a result Observation. Candidate CDISC/NCI terminology for that Observation is C96613 (overall response), C124415 (RECIST 1.1 method) and C35571 (PD result). A generic mCODE Cancer Disease Status Observation, including LOINC 97509-4, does not establish the method. Verify the local fields and source assessment before accepting this proposal.

bindings.fact: Clinical effective date of the same RECIST PD event, available for the screening assessment.
bindings.proposed_source: Use the reviewed malignancy history and the dated imaging or RECIST assessment. Validate the meaning of Observation.effective[x] or DiagnosticReport.effective[x] against the documented progression date. Preserve report issue time and version separately.

bindings.fact: An actual disease-directed treatment course for the index malignancy, including modality, course identity and the event dates needed to establish sequence and recency.
bindings.proposed_source: Review systemic and non-systemic treatment history recorded under §8.2. Candidate records include MedicationAdministration.effective[x] and Procedure.performed[x], with evidence of delivery, indication and course boundaries. Orders alone do not document exposure. A single administration does not establish completion of the entire course.

bindings.fact: Source-supported relationship between the response, the treatment course, the same patient and the malignancy under review.
bindings.proposed_source: Use a reviewed longitudinal oncology treatment/response history or an explicit course-to-assessment reference backed by the historical reports. Preserve patient, malignancy, dates, assessor and versioned source references. Historical evidence may originate in earlier encounters.

bindings.fact: Screening date for this workflow run.
bindings.proposed_source: task.json, screening_clock. Capture the local run date in the screening context.

clinical_questions.question: Does the six-month interval before screening constrain the date of RECIST progression alone, the linked previous treatment event, or both?
clinical_questions.cited_source: Signed protocol v2 / Amendment 1, p. 48, §5.2.3, item 18, especially “after previous treatment within 6 months prior to screening”. Signed protocol, p. 61, §8.2, screening/baseline assessments, final paragraph records both the treatment history and date of last progression.
possible_answers: The progression must be in the interval. The treatment may be older.
The previous treatment event must be in the interval, with subsequent progression before screening.
Both events must be in the interval. With a single treatment event strictly before progression and both before screening, this has the same result as requiring recent treatment.
clinical_questions.discriminating_example: Screening is 15 October 2026. The only course ended 15 February and RECIST 1.1 PD occurred 15 August. The patient meets the progression-only interpretation and fails either interpretation requiring recent treatment.

clinical_questions.question: For a course with repeated administrations, does progression after treatment has begun qualify while that course continues, or must progression follow the last actual administration or the documented end of the course?
clinical_questions.cited_source: Signed protocol v2 / Amendment 1, p. 48, §5.2.3, item 18, “after previous treatment”. Signed protocol, p. 61, §8.2, screening/baseline assessments, final paragraph links treatment to its response but does not name the ordering milestone.
possible_answers: After at least one actual exposure, including PD during the course.
Strictly after the final delivered dose or procedure.
Strictly after the documented end of the course.
clinical_questions.discriminating_example: The only course began 1 July, PD was assessed 20 July, its final dose was 30 July, and screening was 15 October 2026. An exposure-based interpretation accepts this pair. A final-dose or end-of-course interpretation rejects it.

clinical_questions.question: If a patient has received another course since a qualifying progression, can PD associated with an earlier course meet item 18, or must the progression follow the course immediately preceding screening?
clinical_questions.cited_source: Signed protocol v2 / Amendment 1, p. 48, §5.2.3, item 18, “previous treatment”. Signed protocol, p. 61, §8.2, screening/baseline assessments, final paragraph collects prior treatments, their associated responses and the last progression date.
possible_answers: Any linked previous course may qualify.
Only the immediately preceding course may qualify.
clinical_questions.discriminating_example: Course A ended 1 June, with PD on 15 June. Course B ended 31 August with stable disease and no subsequent PD before 15 September screening. All dates are in 2026. An any-course rule qualifies the June event. An immediately-preceding-course rule does not.

rationale: Item 18 permits RECIST 1.1 progression with either measurable or non-measurable disease. The six-month qualifier and the reference treatment event can change eligibility even with complete records. Section 8.2 identifies the relevant history, but the catalog supplies no verified mapping for a dated RECIST assessment, an actual prior course or their association. Both protocol interpretation and evidence binding are required.

terminology_sources.source: Eisenhauer et al., revised RECIST guideline (version 1.1), §§4.3–4.4 and Tables 1–2. Protocol reference 3.
CDISC, Oncology Response Mappings, 2022, slide 11. Candidate terminology for the method, timepoint assessment and result.
HL7 mCODE v4.0.0, Cancer Disease Status Profile. Generic clinical status only.
HL7 FHIR R4, MedicationAdministration. Proposed treatment evidence shape.
HL7 FHIR R4, Procedure. Proposed treatment evidence shape.
